question: Does the Bagac River citation listed as Roque et al. (2019) in the 2026 freshwater-goby synthesis identify a separate primary source, and what can be safely confirmed?

source.citation: Roque, N. B. C., Corpuz, M. N. C., & Manliclic, A. D. C. (2019). Rapid bioassessment and ordination analysis of fish assemblages in Bagac river systems, Bataan, Philippines. Journal on Food, Environment, Engineering and Technology, 2(1), 33–37. 2nd National Conference on Food, Environment, Engineering and Technology proceedings.
source.conferenceLocationAsReported: Crown Royale, Balanga City, Bataan, Philippines
source.accessNote: The full text and Table 1 were reviewed in the author-uploaded ResearchGate copy. No separate publisher-hosted copy or item-specific license was verified. ResearchGate labels the uploaded content as potentially subject to copyright.

studyScope.sourceReportedWaterbodyContext: The paper covers the Bagac river system along a stated five-kilometer stretch and names upstream, midstream, and downstream sections.
studyScope.surveyDesign: The methods report gill netting, seine netting, and a stupefying method, with water and habitat variables recorded for the three river sections. The Results section reports at least 400 individuals, 17 fish taxa, ten families, and five Gobiidae taxa; Table 1 lists 17 source labels with section-level presence/absence.
studyScope.fieldDateLimit: No exact collection dates, event-level records, or station-level coordinates were found in the reviewed paper. The paper gives a single study-area coordinate, which is not a station or fish-capture geometry.
studyScope.tableLimit: The source's names and family assignments are retained as source labels only; no current-name, specimen, or voucher crosswalk was performed.

systematicReviewCrosswalk.secondaryFinding: Baron and Garces (2026), Table 2, lists Roque et al. (2019) for Bagac with 17 fish taxa and five goby taxa, while the paper is absent from its Table 1 bibliography.
systematicReviewCrosswalk.primaryMatch: The author-uploaded 2019 conference paper has the matching title/authors and reports 17 fish taxa in its table and five Gobiidae taxa in its Results. This confirms the identity of the separate 2019 citation and supports the 17/5 summary; it does not resolve the synthesis's 23-versus-27 study-row denominator.
systematicReviewCrosswalk.decision: Keep the 2019 conference paper and the 2022 AACL Bioflux article as distinct source records. The 2022 paper reports 15 taxa and 400 specimens; shared authors, waterbody, and section names leave possible sampling overlap unresolved because neither paper supplies a comparable field-date or specimen crosswalk. Do not merge their tables, totals, or claims.

qualityAndUseLimits: The paper's reported 400-plus individuals and 17 taxa describe one historical survey, not current river abundance or a complete Bataan checklist.
The 2019 paper provides section-level presence/absence but no event dates, station coordinates, or taxon-to-voucher crosswalk; it cannot support point geometry or current presence.
The 2019 and 2022 papers have different reported totals and methods. Their sample independence and overlap are not established.
No item-specific reuse permission or license was located. Do not redistribute the table or promote its rows into public app data until rights and evidence checks are complete.
The paper's Figure 1 is an ordination/cluster plot, not a taxon-identified fish photograph. No fish image was admitted.
nextAction: Keep the source research-only; seek item-specific reuse terms and a field-date/specimen crosswalk if publication use is considered. Continue Central Luzon evidence work with separately dated, named-waterbody sources for Candaba wetlands, reservoirs, rivers, estuaries, and coastal waters.

sources.supports: Author-uploaded 2019 paper identity, conference details, methods, aggregate counts, Table 1, and ResearchGate copyright notice.
The 2026 synthesis's Table 1/Table 2 citation and count discrepancy.
Distinct 2022 Bagac source citation, methods, and 15-taxon/400-specimen abstract summary.
Independent later bibliography corroborating the title, authors, year, and pages of the 2019 proceedings paper.
Independent later bibliography corroborating the 2019 citation and distinguishing it from the 2022 article.
